Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back. The players are out in the middle. Parvez Hossain Emon and Tanzid Hasan to open for Bangladesh. Mujeeb Ur Rahman to bowl first. Let's play...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Well, now Bangladesh have to chase 144! They will be hoping for their batters to complete the clean sweep in this series. For Afghanistan, the onus will be on their bowlers to defend this total and avoid the clean sweep. Can they do it? We shall find out soon. Chase coming up shortly...

Bangladesh were excellent with the ball. Their bowlers struck whenever a partnership was brewing for the Afghan side. Just when Afghanistan's hopes seemed to be fading, they found new life. Rasooli's fighting 32 and Mujeeb's explosive 23 but overall, Bangladesh will be the happier side going into the break. Mohammad Saifuddin was their pick of the bowlers who picked three wickets. Nasum Ahmed and Tanzim Hasan Sakib picked two each while Rishad Hossain and Shoriful Islam chipped in with one each.

Afghanistan end with a fightable total of 143! A massive reprieve from 98/8! It was a tough start for Afghanistan, losing three wickets in an underwhelming powerplay, and managing just 39 runs. Sediqullah Atal and Darwish Rasooli showed some resistance, adding 34 runs together. After their dismissal, it was Mujeeb Ur Rahman who showed some intent and played a cameo of 23 runs to get their side to a fightable total.
A yorker, on middle and leg, Mujeeb Ur Rahman knocks it down the ground for a brace. Afghanistan end their innings at 143/9!

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the game to begin. The umpires and the players are out in the middle. Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Ibrahim Zadran walk in with their blades for Afghanistan. Shoriful Islam has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

Pitch Report - Farveez Mahroof is pitchside. He expects the spinners to thrive on the Sharjah pitch, which has been challenging for batters. He suggests a score of 160-170 will be competitive for Bangladesh.

Rashid Khan, the skipper of Afghanistan, says that they wanted to bat first as its a good track. He says that they need to improve at the start with the bat and the ball in the opening overs. He adds that they have a good backup for each and every player so it gives them a good opportunity and that is the reason they give a chance to the youngsters. Ends by saying that Noor misses out, and Bashir comes in the side.

Jaker Ali, the skipper of Bangladesh, says that its a new wicket and they will bowl first. He adds that as a team, they are happy about the performance so far. He says that Afghanistan has a good side and some world-class spinners and they have done well as a batting side. Ends by saying that Mustafizur Rahman is not playing and Tanzim Hasan Sakib comes in.

Afghanistan (Playing XI) - Sediqullah Atal, Ibrahim Zadran, Rahmanullah Gurbaz (WK), Wafiullah Tarakhil, Darwish Rasooli, Azmatullah Omarzai, Mohammad Nabi, Rashid Khan (C), Abdullah Ahmadzai, Mujeeb Ur Rahman, Bashir Ahmad (In for Noor Ahmad).

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Tanzid Hasan, Parvez Hossain Emon, Saif Hassan, Jaker Ali (C)(WK), Shamim Hossain, Nurul Hasan, Nasum Ahmed, Mohammad Saifuddin, Rishad Hossain, Shoriful Islam, Tanzim Hasan Sakib (In for Mustafizur Rahman).
TOSS - Bangladesh have won the toss and will BOWL first.
So, will Bangladesh secure the clean sweep, or will Afghanistan produce a spectacular upset? Tune in now to see this exciting series finale unfold! Toss and team news in a bit...

The Sharjah pitch has provided a fair contest, where a total around 160-170 has been competitive. Spinners are expected to have a significant role as the game unfolds under the lights, making every run and every wicket a crucial moment. While Bangladesh enters as the favorite, the unpredictability and explosive potential of Afghanistan means nothing is guaranteed.

Bangladesh come into this game with serious momentum, having clinched both previous matches, including a thrilling two-wicket victory in the last over on Friday. Their all-round depth has been on display, but they'll need to be wary of Afghanistan's spin attack, led by Rashid Khan and Mujeeb Ur Rahman, who nearly turned the tide in the second T20I. Keep an eye out for a potential return of the fit-again Bangladeshi batter, Towhid Hridoy, which could further bolster their batting lineup.

Welcome to the final showdown! Get ready for an electrifying third and final T20I between Bangladesh and Afghanistan, live from Sharjah! Tonight promises a clash of contrasting ambitions, for the soaring Tigers, it's a chance to complete a dominant 3-0 clean sweep and stamp their authority on the shortest format. For the determined Afghans, it's an opportunity for a much-needed victory to restore pride after a tough series and show their fighting spirit. The stage is set for a thrilling conclusion to this series.
... MATCH DAY ...

Sharjah sets the stage for the final showdown in the three-match T20I series between Afghanistan and Bangladesh. With Bangladesh already clinching the series 2-0, the third game offers little in terms of stakes but plenty in terms of pride. Afghanistan, despite their fighting spirit, have now suffered four straight defeats in T20Is, and three of them at the hands of Bangladesh. The results highlight just how tough it has been for the Afghans to overcome a Bangladesh side that has looked sharper. The rhythm of a T20 contest in the UAE mirrors an asymmetrical wave of unpredictable, jagged, and without discernible pattern. Momentum surges and collapses without warning, as if the desert air itself conspires to keep logic at bay. In both games, Afghanistan batted first and posted a moderate to a below-par total, in that 145-155 bracket, which proved a little less to defend. However, the Afghans will take heart from the way they fought in the second T20I, almost making Bangladesh huff and puff for every run. Bowling has seldom been Afghanistan’s concern with the luxury and variations of spin they have, led by Rashid Khan. Their attack has consistently delivered under pressure, often keeping games alive with discipline and heart. It is the batting that has faltered - erratic, unreliable, and prone to collapse just when partnerships begin to flourish. The familiar pattern of losing wickets after a promising stand has resurfaced, leaving the top order to carry the weight. Amid the inconsistency, Azmatullah Omarzai has emerged as a genuine all-rounder. He continues to impress with both bat and ball, and his recent four-wicket haul nearly turned the tide against the Tigers, offering a rare moment of defiance in an otherwise uphill battle. One more positive is Rahmanullah Gurbaz returning to form after a sloppy Asia Cup run, but it is all about producing a complete performance across both departments and winning those crucial phases to assert dominance. Meanwhile, Bangladesh have sealed the series with authority, notching up their fourth successive T20I series win. Two of those have come on foreign soil, while two was secured at home. Their bowling has been quietly effective throughout this campaign, never conceding more than 40 runs in the Powerplay and making full use of Sharjah’s slow surface. What has truly stood out is the variety in their attack, blending pace and spin with precision. By dominating the early exchanges, they have consistently taken control of the contest. Taskin Ahmed and Mustafizur Rahman have all contributed with sharp spells, while Nasum Ahmed and Rishad Hossain have strengthened the spin unit with discipline and bite. Litton Das may be absent, but Bangladesh have not felt the void in this series. The top order, led by Parvez Hossain Emon and Tanzid Hasan, has stepped up with assurance. Yet, the middle order remains a concern, as its inconsistency has left Bangladesh with work to do before sterner tests arrive. That area will be a key focus moving forward. As the final T20I approaches, Afghanistan will be eager to restore some pride and avoid a clean sweep, while Bangladesh aim to register their first whitewash in the format this year. With both teams chasing contrasting goals, the stage is set for a compelling finale before the spotlight shifts to the longer white-ball format.
